g.text: A repair must not hide a consequential regression
Compare a vector of quality, critical defects, time and reviewer effort before expanding exposure.
A quality gain cannot offset prohibited access, fabricated support or an unapproved action.

Sofia Jakovcevic’s release describes a prompt repair that improves safety while harming completion. Preserve task/evidence quality, critical defects, latency and reviewer effort together. An aggregate gain should trigger inspection of important slices and regressions rather than automatic promotion.

Omni’s release emphasizes full traces and gates that actually stop work. Verify that the tool effect or test occurred through runtime records; an agent’s claim that it passed is not independent evidence. Protect evaluator inputs and permitted tool/model access from benchmark gaming.

Retain task/data/evaluator versions, failure examples, expert disagreements, accepted exceptions and the owner. Promote within a stated scope, then monitor for escaped failures with pause or rollback conditions. Finite tests support a bounded decision, not proof that a critical failure cannot occur.
Sources: Arize · Omni Analytics · Google DeepMind / Kaggle / LinqAlpha | Reviewed October 25, 2026
